_README: The pinned verify-RED set. Each case BREAKS one guard's decision and names
the test that must notice. CI fails if any case SURVIVES -- that test no
longer pins the property it is named for -- or ABORTS, because a case that
could not run has established nothing.
A case whose mutated run never opened its target ABORTS too: the test does
not load the file, or loaded a copy from outside the sweep's.
Deliberately SMALL. This is not coverage tooling; it is a handful of
load-bearing decisions whose tests must never rot silently.
EVERY PAIRING HERE WAS VERIFIED TO DISCRIMINATE, not assumed. The first
draft of this file had two cases that SURVIVED, and neither was a weak
test: one mutated `main()` while the test calls `_rm_violations` directly,
and the other was behaviourally null -- `rm -rf /` has zero path segments,
so `len(parts) < 4` and `< 1` are both true. A third candidate was masked
by a sibling layer: `_ALWAYS_BLOCK` refuses `/`, `.`, `~` regardless of
depth, so every test using those inputs is structurally blind to the depth
rule. Choose the input that discriminates, then confirm it does.
AN ANCHOR THAT STOPS MATCHING IS A FEATURE. If someone edits a guard and
this gate aborts with 'anchor matched 0x', the case must be updated in the
same change -- exactly the moment to ask whether the test still pins the
new shape.

cases.label: rm-guard depth floor weakened from 4 to 1
cases.why: the depth threshold IS the guard's judgement. A weakened floor still refuses something, so a test asserting only 'blocks at all' would miss it -- this case uses a depth-3 target (~/genesis) precisely because `/` is refused by _ALWAYS_BLOCK regardless of depth and would mask the mutation

cases.label: protected-paths guard stops blocking entirely
cases.why: deleting a protected directory must be refused, and this is the single decision point that refuses it

cases.label: inbox report salvages corrupt versioned input
cases.why: One invalid element makes the entire retained v2 input unknown; no valid-looking URL may be salvaged as evaluated.

cases.label: inbox report promotes cumulative baseline to dispatched input
cases.replacement: and (url in r.item_urls or url in r.baseline_urls)
cases.why: The cumulative baseline may include text appended after dispatch; membership must not create evaluated status.

cases.label: inbox report equates item identity with URL-only identity
cases.why: A stored URL does not prove a changed annotation or whole logical item was handled; all report victims are disposable fixtures.

cases.label: inbox report drops lossy text baseline uncertainty
cases.why: Sorted cumulative lines retain historical appearance without input boundaries; their text-only uncertainty must survive.

cases.label: inbox report treats unknown noncompleted input as never
cases.anchor: row.item_urls is None or url in row.item_urls
cases.why: Missing failed-row input cannot prove that a URL was never dispatched; the fixture has no baseline to mask the fallback.

cases.label: inbox rulings drops exact tag filtering
cases.why: Near-match tags are not owner disposition tags; every database and output is isolated.

cases.label: inbox rulings hides metadata-free history
cases.why: Missing companion metadata must remain visible as uncertain history, never silently disappear.

cases.label: inbox rulings loses snapshot across reads
cases.why: A later fixture WAL writer must not change the active history reader's snapshot; no live store is reachable.

cases.label: manual-only generator drops normal YAML flag
cases.anchor:
manual = loaded.get("disable-model-invocation")
                if manual is True or (isinstance(manual, str) and manual.strip().lower() == "true"):
cases.why: The actual generator-to-hook/executor flow must not suggest or inject a manual-only skill; all catalog/skill files and hook state are isolated.

cases.label: manual-only step guard ignores delegated target
cases.anchor: for name in (skill_name.lower(), delegated_name) if name
cases.why: An ordinary assigned research skill cannot inject a manual-only delegated method; ordinary unmarked delegation remains a positive control.
